articleTitle: A Reconfigurable CMOS Rectifier for 905-MHz RF Energy Harvester with Omnidirectional Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article proposes a high-efficiency reconfigurable CMOS rectifier for radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting. The rectifier has been fabricated in a $180-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS technology. With the auxiliary transistors and substrate technique, working in 905 MHz, the proposed rectifier finally achieves a peak efficiency of 54% under $24-\mathrm{k} \Omega$ loading resistance with the power dynamic range (PDR) of 9.3 dB. Moreover, a $905-\mathrm{MHz}$ RF energy harvester with the proposed rectifier and a wide-band omnidirectional monopole antenna is designed. The proposed antenna bandwidth with $\left|S_{11}\right|\lt-10 \mathrm{~dB}$ is given by 900 MHz, and under the constant distance from transmit antenna to received antenna of 30 cm, the measured harvester output voltage reaches 1 V with -11.7 dBm received RF power.

articleTitle: A Wideband Miniaturized dB-Linear Millimeter-Wave Power Detector in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and validation of a high-performance power detection circuit using a 40 nm CMOS technology, achieving wide dynamic range, high sensitivity, and miniaturization for wideband applications. measurement results demonstrate effective operation over a frequency range of 2-40 GHz, with a minimum detectable power of −33 dBm, and an input range of $-33 \sim 10 \text{dBm}$. The circuit occupies $0.124 \ \text{mm}^{2}$ and consumes 3.85 mW of power.

articleTitle: A 3.4 mW ± 0.45 dB-Gain-Variation 6-10GHz Low-Noise Amplifier with Embedded Capacitive Feedback and RC Extension Network for Gb/s UWB Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband low-noise amplifier with flat in-band gain for 6-10 GHz ultra-wideband high data rate communication application. The embedded capacitive feedback technique is proposed to suppress the current dissipation and noise factor of the input transistor without additional power consumption. The proposed RC extension network provides an extra effective pole to realize wideband flat gain. Fabricated in 65nm CMOS, the LNA achieves a power gain of 12.2-13.1dB across 6-10GHz with ±0.45dB in-band gain variation and 4.3-5.7dB NF. It consumes 3.4mW from a 1.2V supply and occupies a compact die area of 0.094 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: An FPGA-based QDI Asynchronous Circuits Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Quasi delay insensitive (QDI) circuits, as a type of asynchronous circuits, have unique advantages such as high robustness, low power consumption, and event driven, so they have the potential to be applied in fields such as Network-on-Chip (NoC). However, due to the lack of supporting EDA tools, designing QDI circuits is difficult, resulting in limited application. This article proposes a systematic FPGA-based QDI circuit design methodology based on existing EDA tools, and designs a QDI router according to the proposed methodology. The designed QDI router reduces power consumption by 52.1% and latency by 19.7% compared to synchronous router with similar structure.

articleTitle: A 11.4-GHz Dual-Mode Multi-Modulus Divider in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-modulus divider (MMD) designed for a $\mathrm{Ka} / \mathrm{Ku}$-band frequency synthesizer used in satellite communications (SATCOM). The MMD is composed of nine cascaded divide-by- 2/3 cells, with the first cell utilizing a novel current mode logic (CML) structure to improve speed with a limited power supply. The remaining cells employ inverter-latch for simplicity. To achieve a large division ratio range from 128 to 255 and 512 to 1023, a switch signal is inserted to change the number of cascaded divide-by- 2/3 cells. With a delta-sigma modulator (DSM), it can operate in either 7-bit fractional mode or 9-bit integer mode. Embedded in a frequency synthesizer, the proposed dual-mode MMD can support maximum operation frequency up to 11.4 GHz. Fabricated in $65-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS technology, the proposed MMD occupies an area of $0.018 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ and consumes 8.6 mW DC power from a 1 V supply.

articleTitle: A High Frequency Two-Stage Multilevel Converter with a Wide Output Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage multilevel converter which consists of a switched capacitor ladder and a four-phase buck converter. Similar as the classic multilevel converters, this work achieves a wide output range with reduced inductor voltage stress, enabling small inductors and high frequency operations. On the other hand, this work resolves the huge component count require by the typical multiphase multilevel converters, by providing multiple intermediate bus voltages. Therefore, this proposed work achieves a wide output range and high frequency operations with easy multiphase extensions. Designed in a 65 nm CMOS process, the proposed converter achieves a simulated 0.4 V -to- 1.3 V output range and peak efficiency 91.64% under 1.8 V input and 20 MHz single phase buck frequency. For load transient between 0 and 2 A with $2 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{ns}$ speed, the output voltage exhibits $+35 \mathrm{mV} /-35 \mathrm{mV}$ undershoot and overshoot, respectively.

articleTitle: A 4 nW, -77 dBm Sensitivity Wake-up Receiver with Differential Gate-biased Envelope Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-low-power wake-up receiver (WuRX) based on SMIC 55-nm ULP CMOS technology. The receiver front-end utilizes a 25 -stage differential passive envelope detector with gate biasing, eliminating the off-chip balun and enhancing sensitivity. The baseband circuit is improved and designed with a combination of high and low threshold transistors, allowing it to operate at a supply voltage of 0.4 V VDD. The proposed WuRX achieves a sensitivity of -77 dBm and a power consumption of 4 nW at an operating frequency of 915 MHz.

articleTitle: A 0.6-8.1 GHz, 2 dB NF inductorless LNTA in 22 nm CMOS with novel bandwidth extension technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper introduces a broadband low-noise transconductance amplifier (LNTA) d esigned f or s urface a coustic wave (SAW) filter-less wideband receivers (RXs). The design is based on common-source stage with resistive feedback (CS-RF) structure, utilizing the combination of a cascode stage and an auxiliary common-source stage to expand the bandwidth and achieve noise cancellation. The circuit implements derivative superposition by summing currents from transistors with different threshold voltages, thereby enhancing the input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of the LNTA. The overall circuit utilizes a complementary NMOS/PMOS architecture for current reuse, resulting in power savings. The chip is implemented in 22-nm CMOS technology. Post-simulation results indicate that the proposed LNTA achieves a transconductance gain (Gm) of 280 mS and a minimum noise figure (NF) of 2 d B w ithin a b andwidth upto8 G Hz. The maximum IIP3 across various frequency bands reaches $\mathbf{- 1 0. 8} \mathbf{~ d B m}$. Under a 0.9 V power supply, the power consumption is 4.6 mW. The circuit occupies an area of only $120 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 90 \mu \mathrm{~m}$.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Power Timing Based OOK Modulation CMOS Transmitter Applied in RF-Powered Temperature Sensor Node
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient CMOS transmitter (TX) for autonomous temperature sensor nodes. The TX structure is simplified using a frequency divider and power amplifier (PA) with on-off keying (OOK) modulation. A two-stage duty cycle modulator is introduced to significantly reduce power consumption. The $1^{\text {st }}$ stage controls TX operation between active and inactive modes based on energy availability, while the $2^{\text {nd }}$ stage compresses the duty ratio during active mode to further reduce operating time. Finally, a 305 MHz TX system is implemented with a standard $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process. The active area of chip is $0.01 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The supply voltage is 1.2 V. Post simulation results indicate that the power consumption of $862 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ is obtained during data transmission at room temperature. After $1^{\text {st }}$-stage modulation (1 active per 63 dis-active), the average power consumption is reduced to $13.7 \mu \mathrm{~W}$. After both $1^{\text {st }}$ and $2^{\text {nd}}$-stages modulation (277 pulses with pulse width of $1.5 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ in 1 s), the ultimate average power consumption reduces to only 5.9 nW. This ultra-low power performance demonstrates good applicability for wireless sensor network (WSN) applications.

articleTitle: A High Linearity Driver with a Wide Common-Mode Voltage Range in 130-nm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a high linearity and wide input common-mode voltage driver in 130-nm BiCMOS. The driver consisting of the level shifter, continuous time linear equalizer (CTLE), and output driver achieves a tunable peaking gain from 13.5 to 26.9 dB at 30 GHz. The proposed driver featuring wide range linearity enhancement technique achieves a minimum total harmonic distortion (THD) of −63.2 dBc at 5 GHz and a maximum THD of −48.8 dBc at 15 GHz with the input common-mode voltage ranges from 0.2 to 0.7 V.

articleTitle: Specialized Accelerator for Matrix Operation in Robotic Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As a typical operator in robotic control scenarios, matrix operations such as matrix multiplication and matrix inversion have significantly limited the performance of robotic controllers due to high complexity. To accelerate the matrix computation, this paper conducts parallel optimization of matrix algorithms and proposes a heterogeneous matrix computation accelerator which is dynamically reconfigurable for industrial robotic control scenarios involving matrix dimensions between 4 and 9. The design is prototyped on the Xilinx FPGA VCU128 evaluation board with a clock frequency of 250 MHz and synthesized using UMC 40 nm CMOS process at 0.99 V and 500 MHz. Comparisons with the scalar and vector instruction sets of a RISC-V processor indicate that the proposed matrix computation accelerator achieves a speedup of 50.08~143.10 and 10.25~12.36 times for matrix multiplication, 13.65~42.18 and 5.60~10.20 times for dense matrix inversion, and further improved $14.31 \sim 44.60$ and 5.89~10.76 times for sparse matrix inversion.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Monitoring Using FMCW Radar with Dilated Convolutions and Residual Blocks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article introduces an innovative deep learning method for heart rate (HR) detection using a Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar system. The proposed approach seamlessly integrates feature extraction and HR monitoring into a single computational model, thereby eliminating the need for the complex handcrafted feature extraction modules required by previous methods. The system utilizes dilated convolutions and residual blocks to construct the Dilated Residual Convolutional Network (DRCN) model, which directly processes chest micro-motion phase signals obtained from radar data. Experimental results demonstrate that the DRCN model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in HR detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A Clock Generator with Dual Pseudo Random Spread Spectrum in DC-DC Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a spread-spectrum clock generator used in buck converter to realize low electromagnetic interference (EMI) is presented. To make the switching frequency further modulated randomly, dual random spread spectrum effect is implemented by changing the arrays of both current and resistor. The compact circuit achieves $6 \%$ spread of the switching frequency. A DC-DC buck converter with the proposed scheme is designed and fabricated in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m} \mathrm{BCD}$ process for verification. The peak power spectrum is reduced by 15.4 dB with $V_{I N}=12 \mathrm{~V}$ and $V_{\text {out }}=3.6 \mathrm{~V}$.

articleTitle: Amorphous InAIZnO-based 2T0C Unit for Peak Signal Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Real-time peak detection (PD) is a fundamental task in diverse fields ranging from audio processing to telecommunication, where timely and accurate identification of signal peaks is crucial. However, conventional operational amplifier (OPA) based peak detectors suffer from significant hardware overhead and high power-consumption, making them impractical for deployment in edge devices that require low power, small form factors, and high performance. In this work, a novel peak detector based on the amorphous InAIZnO 2T0C DRAM unit is proposed for the first time to facilitate the PD tasks, achieving over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ reduction in hardware overhead compared to conventional OPA-based solutions.

articleTitle: A Rugged 1200V P-channel LDMOS in Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS Process with Global Potential Control Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The ultra-high voltage P-channel later diffused MOS (PLDMOS) is difficult to be integrated in 1200 V high voltage integrated circuits for level-down function, which limits some functions such as high side fault detection to apply. In this work, the global potential control technology solves the problems of leakage increase and on-state current expansion caused by PLDMOS. The isolation structure with embedded PLDMOS achieves off-state breakdown voltage $(B V)$ of 1675 V with a very low leakage current of $0.2 \mathrm{nA} / \mu \mathrm{m}$ at 1200 V, and the on-state BV (at $V_{G S}=-15 V$) of PLDMOS are 1635 V. In addition, the level-down function of fabricated PLDMOS is verified in circuit.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: Design of an RRAM In-Memory Computing Scheme for Target Tracking Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, we present a resistive random-access memory (RRAM) in-memory computing system for object tracking applications. The system includes a $\mathrm{TaO}_{\mathrm{x}}$ RRAM array for storing algorithm data, capable of supporting both binary and multi-level weight storage. We have also designed digital control circuitry based on the RRAM array to interface with a vision sensor chip and the in-memory computing module. By performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations under two different weight storage modes, we obtain the standard deviation from the ideal MAC values and introduce Gaussian noise into the SiamFC object tracking algorithm. The OTB2015 dataset is used to evaluate the two schemes. The results indicate that the algorithm, without error introduction at the software end, achieves an precision of 0.783 and a success rate of $\mathbf{0. 5 8 3}$. When the errors from hardware MAC are introduced, the precision and success rate are 0.781 and 0.582 in the best case, respectively, indicating negligible impact on the algorithm’s performance.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: A Ping-Pong Analog Delta Generator for Delt-Sigma Computing-In-Memory SRAM Macro for Edge AI Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The delta-sigma computing in memory ($\triangle$ CIM) is a promising approach for edge computation, which is beneficial for energy efficiency. Prior research utilized a digital-delta-digitalsigma or digital-delta-analog-sigma computing-in-memory scheme to mitigate this redundant processing, thereby reducing power consumption. This article introduces a dynamic analog ping-pong delta generation to construct an analog-delta-analog-sigma CIM macro. This approach employs a switched capacitor and dynamic amplifier to boost the throughput while maintaining energy efficiency. The simulation demonstrates that our proposed technique can improve throughput and energy efficiency by $\mathbf{2 4 \%}$ and 40%, respectively. The enhanced energy efficiency and computational speed are significant for edge computation devices.

articleTitle: Novel Split-Gate SiC MOSFETs with Fast Switching Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: this paper presents a detailed study of the impact of distance from the Pwell boundary to the polysilicon boundary on the on-resistance, gate oxide electric field and capacitance in splitgate (SG) SiC MOSFET. Based on this analysis, the SG device is prepared, exhibiting a 49% reduction in reverse transfer capacitance $\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{rss}}\right)$ and a 14.2% reduction in gate charge $\left(\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{g}}\right)$ compared to the conventional planar-gate (PG) device. This improvement contributes to a reduction in losses in power electronic systems.

articleTitle: A 92.9dB-SNDR 178.2dB-FoMs SAR ADC with kT/C noise cancellation and FIA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: When designing high resolution ADCs, SAR ADCs face limitations due to sampling $\mathrm{kT} / \mathrm{C}$ noise. The input capacitor size has to be very large. This poses burdens for ADC driver, leading to huge power/area costs and design complexity. We introduce a SAR ADC with noise cancellation and FIA, a fully dynamic amplifier with high power efficiency. A 17-bit SAR ADC was fabricated using a 28 nm CMOS process with a 0.35 MHz bandwidth, achieving 92.9dB SNDR and 178.2dB FoMs in simulation.

articleTitle: AIGaN-Based DUV Micro-PDs and Micro-LEDs: Achieving Superior Emission and Detection Performance Simultaneously
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Advancements in miniaturized optoelectronic devices are crucial for the next generation of lighting, imaging, communication, and sensing technologies. This paper presents a novel micro dual-function diode (DF-diode) that combines light emission and detection capabilities. The DF-diode achieves record-high responsivity in detection mode, with a $300 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{W}$ at 265 nm and a swift 3.7 ns response time. In emission mode, it boasts a −3 dB optical bandwidth surpassing 585 MHz and enhanced external quantum efficiency, showcasing its potential for high-speed and efficient optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Edge-type High-speed Intelligent Infrared Pre-processor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an edge-type high-speed intelligent infrared pre-processor, including the pre-processing algorithm and the corresponding hardware architecture. At algorithm level, guided filtering method and neural network method are combined to propose a non-uniformity correction algorithm with stronger scene adaptability. By combining unsharpen mask and adaptive gray stretching algorithms, the processing effect of image details is effectively improved. At hardware level, this paper optimizes the above algorithm. The structure adopts modular pipeline design, which can realize dynamic switching between algorithms through control instructions, and can effectively meet the real-time pre-processing requirements of infrared images at edge end.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Y-cut LiNbO3 Single Crystalline Film and SAW Resonator on Flexible Polyimide Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Flexible surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators on single crystal LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(LN) film have been successfully fabricated using benzocyclobutene bonding and crystal ion slicing technology. The effects of Polyimide (PI) thickness on the properties of LN film have been studied. 960 nm LN single crystal films without cracks have been transferred to $25 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ PI substrates, which are used to construct flexible SAW resonators. The flexible SAW resonators show well frequency-strain response characteristics. These results demonstrated that LN single crystal film on PI substrate and its SAW resonator is a promising candidate in flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: Prediction of Substrate Warpage by the Trace Mapping and Trace Reinforcement Method During Solder Reflow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the trend of thinning the thickness of package, predicting warpage of substrate accurately is becoming more and more important. However, due to the complex patterns of Cu trace in multiple layers, simulation with high fidelity is extremely costly. In this paper, a novel substrate warpage simulation process using trace reinforcement method is introduced. To estimate the performance of this strategy, models based on trace mapping method are established. Comparing the simulation result of trace reinforcement method with trace mapping method, the accuracy of trace reinforcement method is compatible with trace mapping method with black/white option. With trace reinforcement method, not only the warpage of substrate can be simulated, but also the stress and strain in traces can be obtained.

articleTitle: Fully Pipelined Number Theoretic Transform and Reordering Solution for CRYSTALS-Dilithium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This study presents a fully pipelined hardware architecture for the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT) in the CRYSTALS-Dilithium Post-Quantum Cryptography(PQC) signature algorithm, ensuring an uninterrupted processing flow. Compared to other implementations, experimental results indicate that our design achieves approximately twice the speed of the current fastest solution under conditions with 4 inputs on FPGA platforms. Additionally, the proposed architecture demonstrates superior performance when calculating the Area-Time Product (ATP).

articleTitle: A 470 μW and 875 fps ThroughputJPEG-LS Accelerator in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work presents a low power, high-throughput JPEG-LS accelerator ASIC featuring an 8-stage pipeline architecture and dual-mode computation reuse technology. The chip is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS and occupies $0.71 \ \text{mm}^{2}$ achieving $470 \ \mu \text{W}$ power consumption at 0.8 V supply. With the maximum performance test, this accelerator can achieve a maximum processing speed of 875 fps at a $400 \times 400$ image resolution owing to its 8 -stage pipeline architecture.

articleTitle: A Configurable, Parallel and High-Performance NTT/INTT Accelerator for Post-Quantum Cryptosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: For the post-quantum cryptosystems such as the CRYSTALS-Kyber, the number theoretic transform (NTT) and the inverse number theoretic transform (INTT) are usually adopted as a necessary approach to calculate polynomial multiplications. This paper presents an NTT/INTT accelerator with configurable number of processing element (PE). Varied parameter set (N, q) is supported in the accelerator. A storage-saving scheme for twiddle factors memory is proposed, requiring N/2 storage space only. Implementations under different parameter sets (N, q) on FPGA are described, showing that about $\mathbf{2 5 \%} \sim \mathbf{6 0 \%}$ area-time reduction over many other existing works can be achieved.

articleTitle: A 24V-to-20V Isolated DC-DC Converter with Negative Output Voltage and Continuous Random Spread-Spectrum Modulation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a high-efficiency high-voltage isolated DC-DC converter with positive and negative output voltage for powering isolated gate drivers. A continuous random spread-spectrum modulation(C-RSSM) technique is proposed to mitigate the electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise. Simulation results indicate that the proposed C-RSSM technique reduces the peak of EMI noise spectrum by $14.8 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{~V}$ which is the most effective among various SSM methods. In addition, the converter achieves a peak efficiency of ${7 2. 5} \%$.

articleTitle: A 109.2dB-Dynamic-Range Fully Dynamic Dual-Mode Adjustable Gain Resistive Sensor Interface Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a fully dynamic dual-mode adjustable-gain interface circuit for resistive sensors. This interface circuits are designed with a high input dynamic range (DR) to process general resistive sensors. By adjusting the modulation period of the excitation signal and feedback capacitance of the switched-capacitor circuit, its gain can be tuned accordingly, which thereby enhances the overall DR. By employing different sampling schemes, both bridge resistance and bridge voltage can be measured. A dynamic amplifier is implemented to efficiently enable the proposed dual-mode operations. The proposed circuit was designed, and simulated using 180 nm CMOS technology. The DR enhancement technique provides an additional input range of approximately 50 dB with high SNDR, and an expanded range of 60 to 80 dB with a measurement accuracy of 1%.

articleTitle: A 2.79 μVrms Noise, 3.6 ppm/°C TC Bandgap Reference for Portable Biopotential Signal Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A low-offset, low-noise, high-precision bandgap reference (BGR) for portable biopotential signal monitoring systems is proposed in this paper. Using feedback enhancement technology, the offset voltage and noise of the op-amp are reduced by approximately 23 times when equivalent to the reference output compared to the traditional structure. To reduce the deviation of the reference output under various corners and device mismatch, high-precision base current compensation technology is also adopted. The proposed BGR is implemented using the $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS technology, with a chip area of $0.142 \times 0.258 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The test results indicate that the BGR outputs a 0.6 V reference voltage at a power supply of 1.2V, with a current consumption of $31 \mu \mathrm{~A}$. The integrated noise of $0.1 \sim 10 \mathrm{~Hz}$ is $2.79 \mu V_{\text {rms }}$. The output voltage’s temperature coefficient (TC) is $3.6 \mathrm{ppm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in the range of $-40 \sim 125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: A 50-Gbaud Linear Burst-Mode Trans-Impedance Amplifier in 28 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: this paper presents a 50-Gbaud linear burst-mode (BM) trans-impedance amplifier (TIA) implemented in $28-\mathrm{nm}$ bulk CMOS. Through the introduction of an auxiliary path and a high-speed offset-independent peak detector, the TIA incorporates a BM automatic gain control (AGC) system, capable of processing a 50-Gbaud ‘ 0101 ‘ pattern preamble. Additionally, a dual-mode structure is employed to extend the TIA’s dynamic range. Post-layout simulations demonstrate a dynamic range of 20 dB with a lock time of 100 ns. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a 50 -Gbaud linear BM TIA in CMOS technology.

articleTitle: A Computing In Memory Scheme Using Unipolar Switching SOT-MRAM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an arithmetic paradigm for computing in memory (CIM) using unipolar switching spin-orbit-torque magnetic random access memory (SOT-MRAM) devices. The proposed MRAM array comprises two transistors and one SOT magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) cell and achieves basic Boolean logic operations (AND, XOR, OR, Majority) and full-adder operations. The hybrid spintronics/CMOS simulation results show that the proposed designs improve latency and energy consumption by about $34 \% \sim 132 \%$ and $212 \% \sim \mathbf{4 8 9 \%}$ compared to the existing design, respectively. Monte Carlo simulations further prove the robustness of our design.

articleTitle: A 0.81 ppm/°C, 11.7 μA Voltage Mode Bandgap Reference with Vth-based Piecewise Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a threshold voltage based ($\mathrm{V}_{\text {th }}$-based) piecewise compensated voltage-mode bandgap reference (BGR) with low temperature coefficient (TC) and low current consumption for high precision applications. The $V_{\text {th }}$-based piecewise compensation ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{th}}-\mathrm{PC}$) circuit utilizes the principle that the magnitude of threshold voltage $\left(V_{t h}\right)$ varies with the size of the MOS transistor. It generates piecewise compensation current by comparing the thermal voltage $\left(V_{T}\right)$ term and the $V_{\text {th }}$ term instead of comparing currents, effectively reducing current consumption. Designed in 180 nm CMOS technology, the simulated reference voltage ($V_{\text {REF }}$) of the BGR is ${1. 2 1} \mathrm{V}$, with the TC of $0.81 \mathrm{ppm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for TT process corner from $-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. After trimming, the TC of $V_{\text {REF }}$ is $0.98 \mathrm{ppm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $1.51 \mathrm{ppm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for FF and SS process corner, respectively. The total current consumption is only $11.7 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ at room temperature with a line regulation (LR) of $0.035 \% / \mathrm{V}$.

articleTitle: A 91.7dB-SNDR 5kHz BW 18.5μW PPD-based Single-OTA Zoom ADC using CLS-enhanced Inverter Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a pseudo-pseudo-differential (PPD)--based single-OTA 2nd-order zoom ADC, which employs a 4-bit SAR conversion followed by a 2 nd-order $\Delta \Sigma$ modulator using a single-OTA. The PPD technique significantly minimizes the OTA noise at low frequencies. A CLS-enhanced cascode inverter is proposed as the OTA, boosting its DC gain to 75dB to meet structural requirements. The chip, designed in a 55nm CMOS process with a 1V supply, achieves a 91.7dB SNDR while consuming $18.5 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ at a signal bandwidth 0 f 5 kHz, resulting in a Schreier figure-of-merit (FoM) of 176.0 dB.

articleTitle: A RISC-V Processor with Custom Instructions for Spiking Neural Network Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) have seen widespread applications thanks to their higher energy efficiency compared to artificial neural networks (ANNs). However, hardware accelerators dedicated to SNNs without a CPU generally suffer from a lack of flexibility. In this paper, we present a general-purpose RISC-V processor with extended custom instructions designed to efficiently accelerate SNNs. These custom instructions are executed on a tightly-coupled coprocessor, which is a systolic neuron array. This processor with the coprocessor achieves a speedup of $72 \times$ compared to the version without the coprocessor. When implemented on FPGA, the LUT and REG overhead of the coprocessor is about 30% and 22%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Series-Fed Comb-Array Antenna with Microbumps for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel series-fed comb-array antenna with microbumps based on high resistivity silicon (HRSi) is proposed for sub-Terahertz (THz) applications. The proposed antenna consists of eight circular patches as the radiating elements which are serially fed by a microstrip line. Eight microbumps in flip-chip technology are bonded on the circular patches to achieve a high gain and a high radiation efficiency w ithout a complex manufacturing process and high cost. The microstrip feed line is specially designed according to Chebyshev distribution for sidelobe level (SLL) suppression.

articleTitle: A 0.9-V Supply Up to 21.5-dB Boost Gain Analog Front-End with T-coilloaded CTLE and VGA in 28-nm CMOS for 112-Gb/s PAM-4 Medium-Reach Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an analog front-end (AFE) circuit for 112-Gb/s four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) medium-reach (MR) receivers. To ensure sufficient bandwidth and enhance boost gain, the AFE employs of a cascaded architecture of two stages of continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) and three stages of variable gain amplifier (VGA). Both the CTLE and VGA are loaded with T-coils to extend the bandwidth, enabling the AFE to operate at a standard voltage of 0.9 V without a dedicated regulator. Eight parameters are adopted to tune the high, medium, and low-frequency-bands response to match loss profiles well for MR channels. Post-layout simulations in 28-nm CMOS technology demonstrate that the proposed AFE achieves a gain boost of up to 21.5 dB dissipating 43.8 mW at a 0.9V supply, achieving larger than $28-\mathrm{GHz}$ bandwidth within the area of $0.06 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. When combined with an ideal 4-tap feed-forward equalizer (FFE) from the transmitter, the proposed AFE achieves a symbol error rate $(S E R)\lt 10^{-12}$ at $112 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ using $2^{15}-1$ PRBS PAM-4 pattern with a $19.5-\mathrm{dB}$ channel loss at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-assisted Multiobjective Optimization of Tin-based Perovskite Polycrystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Thin film transistors (TFTs) possess a structural distinction from conventional silicon-based chips. Tin-based perovskites exhibit outstanding optoelectronic properties, convenient processing methods, and cost-effective production. Notably, their nearly negligible ion migration and high carrier mobility at room temperature position them as excellent candidate materials for TFTs. Nevertheless, reproducing high-quality tin-based films remains challenging due to the stringent preparation conditions and process parameters involved. We incorporated machine learning to aid in the optimization of film properties, utilizing Bayesian optimization to adjust HyperParameters. This approach maximizes the utilization of experimental data, narrowing the solution space and enabling simultaneous optimization of multiple indicators. Consequently, we successfully prepared high-quality all-inorganic tin-based perovskite films within a short experimental period. The crystal morphology and photoelectric properties of the films exhibited significant improvements compared to manually optimized results. This work offers a novel and efficient optimization strategy for exploring high-quality new semiconductor films.

articleTitle: A 480W 40-to-60VIN Quadrangle Controlled Four-Switch Buck-Boost Converter with Zero-Freewheeling and Reverse Inductor Current Supply Techniques Achieving 99% Peak Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a quadrangle controlled four-switch buck-boost(FSBB) converter with zero-freewheeling and reverse inductor current supply techniques. With the proposed zero-free-wheeling technique, the ripple of inductor current has been significantly reduced, and freewheeling current has been virtually eliminated, thereby improving light load efficiency. Furthermore, utilizing the inductor reverse current to generate the required 5 V power supply for driving the power transistors, which significantly improves the efficiency of the FSBB converter. Simulation results show that the FSBB converter achieves a peak efficiency of $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$, maintaining efficiencies above $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$ across both full load and input ranges.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Buck-Boost Converter with Stacked Resonant Technology for Dual-Polarity Thermoelectric and Photovoltaic Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an energy harvesting interface for simultaneous extraction of dual-polarity thermoelectric generators (TEG) and photovoltaic cells (PV). The reconfigurable buck-boost converter topology is employed to convert positive or negative input voltages into positive output voltages. Compared to the single-source mode, the proposed double-stacking resonant mode (DSRM) increases the conversion efficiency by 5.6% with the same number of switch transitions for synchronous extraction of negative polarity TEG and PV. Utilizing adaptive impedance matching technology, the proposed adaptive maximum power point tracking controller achieves tracking efficiencies ${\gt}\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ in an ultra-wide range of source resistance (10-1500 $\Omega$). Implementation of the converter is carried out in the $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ process. As demonstrated by simulation results, the peak conversion efficiency of 88.3% is achieved in the DSRM.

articleTitle: A 3μm Pixel Device for Peak Power Mitigation of Global-Shutter Indirect Time of Flight Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a $3 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ pinned photodiode(PPD) pixel device for global-shutter indirect time of flight(iToF) sensor. A trapezoidal-shaped PD-layer and a non-uniform doped charge transfer gate channel are proposed to improve the charge transfer speed and efficiency, which adapt with higher threshold voltage of charge transfer transistor(TX) to reduce the leakage. As a result, the amplitude of TX gate voltage can be reduced, avoiding negative voltage. The proposed pixel device has been designed in a $0.15 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS image sensor(CIS) process. The simulation results show that full-well capacity (FWC) achieves 12233 e -, with the charge transfer time of 3.33 ns. The high/low level gate voltage of TX can be reduced to $2.9 / 0 \mathrm{~V}$, which is helpful to mitigate the peak power of global-shutter iToF sensor.

articleTitle: Cache-Like Dual-Port SOT-MRAM with Read-while-Write Access Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (SOT-MRAM) attracts considerable attention for its cache-like access speed, low energy consumption, and separated read and write paths. The paper proposes a read-while-write (RWW) scheme for a dual-port SOT-MRAM to enable simultaneous read-write operations. We utilize the write voltage division on the track layer to enable 71-fJ read operation while writing in the identical bit-cell. This approach minimizes the impact of write delays on system performance and significantly enhances throughput. Simulation results conducted on an industrial 40-nm CMOS process, demonstrate a throughput improvement of over $60 \%$ in the operational mode of alternate 5-ns write and 3-ns read functionality. Assisting with write verification, the RWW scheme achieves $39 \%$ energy saving in repeated writing, as well as 98.9% access yield.

articleTitle: A 0.5V 18.6nW Bandgap Voltage Reference with A Low-Leakage Sample / Hold Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Low-Leakage sampling/holding (S/H) circuit-based Bandgap reference (BGR) with ultra-low power and low supply voltage. Power consumption is reduced through periodic sampling. A $2 \times$ charge pump (CP) is used to supply the BJT, which relaxes the supply voltage to 0.45 V. An automatic tuning circuit is implemented to maintain the accuracy and temperature coefficient (TC) across varying temperatures. The proposed design is fabricated in a 55 nm CMOS process and the measurement results show that the proposed BGR consumes only 18.6 nW at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, achieving a TC of $25 \mathrm{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ over a temperature range of $-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ at 0.45 V. The line regulation is $0.19 \mathrm{~V} / \%$ from 0.45 V to 1 V.

articleTitle: An Adaptive AFE Circuit to Minimize the Zero-Flow Error in Transit-Time Ultrasonic Water Flowmeter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive analog front end (AFE) circuit for ultrasonic water flowmeter application, including a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) and a low delay dispersion comparator (LDD-CMP). The gain of the PGA is adaptively controlled by a peak detector to minimize the input amplitude variation of the comparator. As to the LDD-CMP, an adaptive current regulating circuit is designed for the conventional two-stage open-loop comparator to reduce the propagation delay dispersion caused by the different input overdrive. The proposed AFE has been fabricated in a $180-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS technology, and the measurement results show that the zero-flow error of the ultrasonic flowmeter ASIC with the proposed AFE is only $6.3 \%$ of that of the one with a conventional comparator, and $6.2 \%$ of the commercial product TDC-GP22, with input frequency at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: CongestionNet: VLSI Congestion Prediction Model Using sFCN with MixConv Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As IC manufacturing technology advances, the scale and complexity of design rules imposed by manufacturers have increased significantly. The modern Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) has a complicated Placement and Routing (P&R) process, which demands multiple iterations to complete the task. This paper introduces a novel model framework, CongestionNet, based on symmetric Fully Convolutional Network (sFCN) to predict congestion hotspots in routing. This model employs MixConv layers and skipped connections to enhance prediction accuracy. Experimental results show that CongestionNet’s Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) reaches $\mathbf{0. 7 3 7 5}$ on ISPD2015 (19% better than existing models), and 0.7935 on CircuitNet-N28 (% better than existing models) respectively. Moreover, with GPU-accelerated prediction method, this model achieves a speed-up ratio of $1,231,557 x$ compared to Cadence Innovus, and a ratio of $1.8 x$ compared to existing deep learning models respectively. To our knowledge, this model is the most accurate FCN-based congestion prediction model in the world and it can greatly assist VLSI back-end designs by significantly shortening convergence time.

articleTitle: An FVF-LDO with Differential EA and Push-Pull Super Source Follower for Fast Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article presents a fully integrated flipped voltage follower (FVF) based low-dropout (LDO) regulator with enhanced transient response for noise-sensitive circuits. Focusing on shorter overshoot response and recovery time, a dual-loop FVF LDO with differential error amplifier (EA) and a push-pull super source follower (PPSSF) is proposed. This work, designed in a 65 nm CMOS process, with 1.2 V input and 1 V output, exhibits a quiescent current ($\text{I}_{\text{Q}}$) of $110 \ \mu \text{A}$. The load current ILOAD ranges from 0 to 20 mA. The circuit achieves 1 ns response time and 122 ns recovery time for both voltage overshoot and undershoot. Furthermore, with 50 dB of DC gain, the LDO reaches a low-frequency power supply rejection (PSR) of -50 dB and the worst full-spectrum PSR of −5.6 dB at 20 mA ILOAD with a 300 pF on-chip capacitor.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Power-Efficient Stacked Differential Transimpedance Amplifier in 0.18-μm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a stacked differential CMOS Transimpedance Amplifier (TIA) with DC-coupled connections to the cathode and anode of a photodiode (PD). It receives naturally differential signals from both ends of the PD, achieving a gain that is twice that of conventional single-ended TIA while reducing the input-referred noise by a factor of $\sqrt{ } 2$. Additionally, by employing voltage domain stacking to reuse the current, the circuit allows for reverse biasing of the PD and improves energy efficiency from 55% to ${9 7 \%}$. We have validated the feasibility of this TIA topology using a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. The implemented TIA operates with a conventional 3.3 V supply voltage, consuming 89.1 mW, and features a differential gain of $70 \mathrm{~dB} \Omega$, an input-referred noise of $7.09 \mathrm{pA} / \sqrt{ } \mathrm{Hz}$, and a 3-dB bandwidth of 6 GHz. To the authors’ best knowledge, this is the first differential TIA for DC coupling with single-ended PD.

articleTitle: High-resolution Stereo-vision Depth Processor with Min-pooling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: High-resolution stereo-vision depth processor is widely adopted due to its cost-effectiveness and high information density. However, higher resolution demands significantly increase on hardware performance requirements. To address this challenge, the proposed Semi-global Matching (SGM) method with min-pooling effectively reduces memory usage by 50%. This optimization enables the achievement of state-of-the-art performance in both FPGA and ASIC implementations while minimizing memory resource consumption.

articleTitle: A 2.69 ppm/°C Bandgap Reference with 42 ppm/V Line Sensitivity for Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision bandgap reference (BGR) with an ultra-low temperature coefficient (TC), line sensitivity (LS) and designable reference voltage for battery management system (BMS) applications. A low dropout regulator (LDO) is employed at the output to compensate for the limited driving capability of the current-mode BGR, while a pre-regulator circuit is implemented to improve its LS. In order to achieve a low TC, piecewise curvature compensation is used to compensate for the higher-order nonlinearity of the $V_{\mathrm{BE}}$ voltage, and two-point trimming at $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $60^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is used to ensure the effectiveness of piecewise curvature compensation under batch trimming. The BGR was implemented in a 180 nm process with an active area of $0.548 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. Measurement results indicate that this BGR has an output voltage of 2.5 V and consumes $84 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ of current at a 5 V supply voltage. An average TC of $2.69 \mathrm{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ with two-point trimming over the temperature range of $-40{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $125{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The proposed BGR can deliver a load current of 1 mA with an LS of $0.0042 \% / V$.

articleTitle: A Battery-Free Wireless Temperature Sensing Chip for Food Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work presents a battery-free wireless temperature sensing chip for long-termly monitoring the food production environment. A calibrated oscillator-based CMOS temperature sensor is proposed instead of the ADC-based power-hungry circuits in conventional works. In addition, the sensor chip can harvest the power transferred by a remote reader to eliminate the use of battery. Meanwhile, the system conduct wireless bidirectional communication between the sensor chip and reader. In this way, the temperature sensing chip is fabricated in 55 nm CMOS process, and the reader chip is implemented in 65 nm CMOS technology. Experimental results show that the temperature measurement error achieves $\pm 1.6^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ from $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, with battery-free readout by a remote reader.

articleTitle: Self-Tracking Zero-Current Detection Based on Switching Node Ringing for High-Current Buck Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A self-tracking zero-current detection (ZCD) for buck converters is presented. The proposed scheme detects the switching node ringing and adaptively adjusts the turn-off time of the low-side switch to achieve accurate ZCD. It combines the advantages of two traditional methods: Zero-I Cross Detector and CCM/DCM Boundary Detector. It is particularly suitable for DC-DC converters with heavy load current applications. Based on a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ BCD process, the proposed ZCD is verified in a 12 A buck converter with $4.5 \mathrm{~m} \Omega$ low-side power switch.

articleTitle: A Configurable EEG Procesing Driver Chip for Wireless Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a Brain Computer Interface (BCI) chip for wearable EEG processing devices, with functions of EEG preprocessing like fixed and configurable band filtering, mean calculation and baseline correction etc., as well as functions of interfacing the ADC and blue tooth modules. Approximate compressors and circuits are applied in the chip design for better delay-area-power efficiency, with the addition of the clock gating scheme, more reduction of power is achieved. The fixed band filters and configurable IIR band filters provides the chip more flexibility in feature extractions. The host computer can configure the chip with custom parameters and commands via the blue tooth module, and the processed data can be sent back reversely. Fabricated in 130 CMOS, the chip was measured individually and in the test board of the wearable device prototype. The proposed chip can operate from the supply of 1.5 V to 0.5 V, and it consumes only 1 mW at $0.85 \text{V}, 2 \text{MHz}$, with valid interactions to the test board.

articleTitle: High-speed Memristive Walsh-Hadamard Transform for Image Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Image compression has a wide range of applications at the edge and has high requirements for real-time performance. Here, we propose a high-speed memristive Walsh-Hadamard Transform (WHT) system based on the pipeline method for image compression, which performs multiple matrix multiplication operations at the same time. The proposed memristive WHT system improves $4 \times$ time efficiency compared to the system without the pipeline method. Our work suggests a promising hardware solution for image compression in future edge computing.

articleTitle: Efficient Hardware Platform Architecture for High-Precision Stereo Vision Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: To achieve high-precision and efficient endoscopic measurement, this study introduces a highly parallel hardware architecture dedicated to the implementation of binocular stereo matching algorithms, aiming to enhance real-time performance while ensuring accuracy. The system employs a combination of the CENSUS and local-expansion (LE) algorithms for precise disparity extraction. Through pipeline design and optimized memory partitioning, we have enabled efficient parallel operation of various system modules. Experimental results demonstrate that the pipeline implementation increases the processing speed by $\mathbf{1 0 7. 3 \%}$ compared to the serial implementation. On the medical dataset SERV-CT, our algorithm exhibits the highest accuracy. Furthermore, the universality of this hardware architecture allows it to adapt to the implementation of various traditional algorithms, thereby enhancing the system’s applicability and scalability.

articleTitle: 130 GBaud PAM-4 1-to-4 Analog Demultiplexer for Wireline and Optical Receivers in 130-nm SiGe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 130 GBaud PAM-4 1-to-4 analog demultiplexer (ADEMUX) in 130-nm SiGe process is presented. Continuous-time linear equalizers (CTLE) are implemented at both the input and output stages to compensate for the channel insertion loss (IL). To eliminate the noise feedthrough of the track-and-hold amplifier (THA), an improved topology based on feedforward capacitors is proposed, which employs smaller capacitors than the conventional topologies to further extend the bandwidth. Simulation results show that the ADEMUX is capable of demultiplexing 130-GBaud PAM4 signaling. The core of ADEMUX dissipates 1.98 W power from a 3.3 V supply.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Memory Architecture with LPDDR4 Extensions for Edge Generative AI Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Edge Generative AI (Gen-AI) inference has become prevalent in every aspect of the society. Present flagship edge products, however, fail to achieve high performance on Gen-AI models for the sake of limited bandwidth. An LPDDR4 compliant intelligent memory architecture is proposed in this paper to accelerate edge Gen-AI while maintaining regular LPDDR4 functions. Simulation shows the proposed architecture performs several times better than flagship products on Gen-AI, showing promise of this near-memory processing architecture.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient and Fault-Tolerant Sparse Coding for Spiking Neural Networks Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) exhibit superior energy efficiency and fault tolerance compared to Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). Due to their spike-based nature, input signals must be encoded into spike trains. However, traditional spiking coding schemes often encounter a trade-off between energy efficiency and fault tolerance. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel coding scheme, Spiking Sparse Coding (SSC), which achieves both high sparsity and enhanced fault tolerance. SSC not only improves network performance but also reduces the number of spikes by 93.69%, resulting in a 76.47% increase in energy efficiency. Additionally, SSC enhances network fault tolerance, with accuracy improvements of up to 12.06% under identical noise interference conditions. We deployed the network on the ZCU102 FPGA platform, operating at a frequency of 200 MHz with a power consumption of 409 mW. On the MNIST dataset, we achieved a classification accuracy of 95.84%. The training speed and energy consumption were 12656 frames per second and 0.032 mJ per image, the inference speed and energy consumption were 19279 frames per second and 0.021 mJ per image.

articleTitle: An Area-Efficient Ising Machine based on Parallel Stochastic Cellular Automata Tempering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As a potential solver for combinatorial optimization problems (COPs), the convergence speed and accuracy of Ising machines still have room to be improved at the level of algorithm and architecture design. In this paper, a novel parallel stochastic cellular automata tempering (PSCAT) algorithm is proposed to enhance the performance of fully-connected Ising machines. Additionally, a modified temperature exchange probability is applied to reduce the number of replicas in the hardware implementation. The utilization of the spin update module is improved by reducing the flip decision block. The design prototype with 2,048 spins and 8 replicas is validated on FPGA. Using the K2000 max-cut problem as a benchmark, our design achieves a solution accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 9 4 \%}$ within 0.5 ms, which is higher than two state-of-the-art works.

articleTitle: A 5.24nW-77.2dBm-Sensitivity Wake-Up Receiver with Global Digital Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a −77.2 dBm sensitivity, 5.24 nW power consumption, and wide temperature range wake-up receiver (WuRX) for wireless sensor networks (WSNs). A global digital temperature compensation (GDTC) technology based on a gate leakage-based sensor is proposed, which achieves the low-power temperature compensation for all key modules. At a supply voltage of 0.4 V and an input RF power of ${- 7 6} \mathrm{dBm}$ at 915 MHz, the $S 11$ variation of the proposed WuRX is reduced by $67 \%$ when temperature changes from $-30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $70^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: 22 nm Ultra-Low Power MCU with 43.5nW/KB Sleep Retention Power for Automotive Grade-1 Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the increasing demand for edge devices, microcontroller unit (MCU) is widely utilized in Automotive Grade-1 applications with its mature architecture and ultra-low power consumption. The expansion of application scenarios imposes greater demands on operating temperature, standby power consumption and data retention time. This paper decomposes the main sources of MCU power consumption and proposes low-power design methodology, including low-leakage retention Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) and optimized clock-tree generation scheme. The MCU is implemented using an industrial 22 nm process. Silicon results show that the hierarchical level of clock tree exhibit a 16.7% reduction compared to the standard flow. The overall SRAM leakage current decreases 59% compared with the scheme without such method. Silicon results demonstrate the operating power consumption is less than $485.92 \mu \mathrm{~W}$, and the leakage current is less than 484.8 nA in the sleep mode.

articleTitle: Forming-free, Uniform, and Multi-level Resistive Switching in W/AlOxNy/Al2O3/Pt Memristor by Nitrogen Annealing Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: By employing a nitrogen annealing strategy, we fabricated $\text{W} / \text{AlO}_{x} \ \text{N}_{y} / \text{Al}_{2} \text{O}_{3} / \text{Pt}$ bipolar memristor with a gradient distribution of nitrogen and oxygen concentrations. Annealing after deposition at $350{ }^{\circ} \text{C}$ introduces vacancies and repairs lattice damage, significantly enhancing device performance. The device demonstrates forming-free resistive switching behaviors with uniform cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device distributions, high endurance ($10^{8}$ cycles), robust retention ($3 \times 10^{3} \ \text{s} \text{@}$ RT and 350 K), and large memory window ($10^{4}$). Moreover, 3-bit resistance states programing positioning the device as a competitive candidate for neuromorphic computing applications. This nitrogen annealing strategy offers a low-cost and general approach to performance enhancement of other metal-oxide memristors.

articleTitle: A 63dB Gain Range with 0.4dB Gain Error dB-Linear Programmable Gain Amplifier Using Cell-Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The increasing demand for wireless and wireline transceivers necessitates a wide gain range and an accurate decibel (dB)-linear characteristic programmable-gain amplifier (PGA). We propose a five-stage “cell-based” PGA that combines four-stage coarse gain amplifiers and one-stage fine gain amplifier, eliminating the need for an additional exponential generator or complex digital processing circuit. Implemented in 65nm CMOS technology, the PGA achieves a gain range from 3.23dB to 66.06 dB with a gain error of less than $\pm 0.4 \mathrm{~dB}$. It also demonstrates a figure of merit (FOM) of 95.5 K, while consuming 1.06 mW of power consumption.

articleTitle: A 154 FPS Efficient Single-frame Bundle Adjustment Accelerator for High Frame Rate Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper enhances the efficiency of Visual Odometry (VO) for mobile robots and vehicles by implementing single-frame Bundle Adjustment (BA) on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). A multi-level reuse hardware architecture is proposed that optimizes the update of the Jacobian matrix and equation solving and helps in reducing FPGA hardware resources and power. Using a parallelizable equation solver, our approach achieves a processing speed of 154 frames per second—2.65 times faster than high-performance CPUs and reduces energy consumption by 8.52 times. Tested on the KITTI dataset, the proposed system reported an average translational error of $1.1 \%$ and a rotational error of $0.0041 \text{deg} / \text{m}$. The results demonstrate FPGAs’, potential to improve VO systems in complex environments.

articleTitle: A Biofuel-Cell-based Energy Harvester with 91% Peak Efficiency and Inherent Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a self-powered biosensing system based on biofuel cells (BFCs) for the simultaneous battery charging and inherent glucose/lactate sensing. The proposed boost converter performs maximum power point (MPP) tracking and power conversion from $0.15-0.6 \mathrm{~V}$ to $3.7-4.2 \mathrm{~V}$ (suitable for battery charging), while establishing a linear relationship between the BFC voltage at MPP and the conversion frequency. This enables the incorporation of the real-time sensing of glucose/lactate concentrations into the power converter, removing the need for separate sensing circuits and minimizing overheads. Simulated in 180 nm CMOS process, the system achieves the energy harvesting of $0.3-0.7 \mathrm{~mW}$ at $2.5-15 \mathrm{mM}$ lactate/glucose, while performing biosensing simultaneously. The boost converter peak efficiency is ${9 1 \%}$ for charging battery at 4V from a BFC MPP voltage of 0.29V.

articleTitle: A PVT-Insensitive Ultra-Low Voltage Wakeup Timer With a Capacitance Multiplier Based Hybrid Reconfigurable FLL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Modern IoT nodes require wake-up timers with ultra-low power consumption. Different from previous works, this work proposes an ultra-low power wake-up timer that can operate at a supply voltage as low as 0.3 V with PVT-insensitive operation. The circuit is based on a hybrid digital-analog reconfigurable FLL with a capacitance multiplier to reduce power consumption and area overhead. Designed in 65 nm CMOS process, the circuit demonstrates a power consumption of 938 nW at 0.3 V supply. A temperature coefficient of $67.5 \text{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \text{C}$, and a line sensitivity of $1.19 \% / \text{V}$ are simulated in the temperature/supply range of $0-100^{\circ} \text{C}$ and $0.3-0.6 \ \text{V}$, respectively.

articleTitle: Hot Carrier Injection Induced Degradation of 14 nm FinFET under High Source-Drain Voltage Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, the degradation of 14 nm FinFET under hot carrier injection (HCI) with high source-drain voltage was investigated. The key transport parameters before and after HCI were extracted from the experimental $I-V$ curves. The degradation laws of transport parameters with stress time and were studied and compared. The degradation of threshold voltage and effective DIBL is mainly controlled by oxide traps, and the degradation of subthreshold swing and mobility is mainly controlled by interface traps. The relationship between degradation rate and stress voltage is further analyzed.

articleTitle: Design Technology Co-Optimization for Memristor Self-Write Termination Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The variations of memristors can cause a degradation of computational precision in the compute-in-memory (CIM), consistently impeding the deployment of CIM applications. The random growth of conductive filaments is an intrinsic property, so that the variation is difficult to overcome through fabrications. Nonetheless, this study offers a viable approach to mitigating variation through the design of circuit and technology co-optimization (DTCO). By integrating the HfOx/AlOy superlattice-like device fabrication with a feedback circuit, this work has achieved the precise self-write termination of the memristor resistance. The results of test demonstrate that the superlattice-like memristors exhibit favorable gradual resistance change, which makes the feedback circuitry adjust the resistance in time. In comparison to the write-verification, this self-write termination has minimized variations and boosted endurance effectively.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: A Multi-Phase Multi-Ratio Resonant Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Converter with Improved Power Density
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a resonant switched-capacitor (ReSC) DC-DC converter for on-chip supply-scaling applications. The proposed DC-DC topology utilizes an arithmetic progression (AP) SC structure and features efficient conversions over wide output-voltage and load-current ranges through multi-mode and multi-phase operations. Specifically, our converter operates in 2phase mode and 5-phase mode under heavy-load and light-load conditions, respectively, to reduce inductor current ripple and switching loss. Implemented in a $65-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS process with an estimated silicon area of $3 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$, the proposed converter can regulate an output of 0.5 V to 1.2 V from an input of 1.5 V. The simulated steady-state peak efficiency is 92.84% and the achievable maximum on-chip power density is $0.67 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}$ with a load current of up to 3 A.

articleTitle: INVITED PAPER: A 21.5-to-37 GHz Series Doherty CMOS Power Amplifier with Distributed Multi-step Impedance Inverting Network Achieving 28.2%/23.2%/13.2% Peak/OP1dB/6dBPBO PAEs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A two-way series Doherty-PA(DPA) with a distributed impedance inverting network (IIN) for millimeter wave applications is presented in this paper. The proposed distributed IIN contributes to achieve wideband linear and PBO efficiency enhancement. Implemented in 65 nm bulk CMOS technology, this work realizes a measured 3 dB bandwidth of 15.5 GHz with 21.2 dB peak small-signal gain at $\mathbf{3 4. 2} \mathbf{G H z}$. Under $1-\mathrm{V}$ power supply, it achieves OP $_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$ over 13.4 dBm and $P_{\text {sat }}$ over 16 dBm between 21-to-30 GHz. The measured maximum $P_{\text {sat }}$, $\mathbf{O P}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$, peak $/ \mathrm{OP}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}} / 6 \mathrm{~dB}_{\text {PBo }} \mathrm{PAE}$ results are $17.5 \mathrm{dBm}, 14.7 \mathrm{dBm}$, and $\mathbf{2 8. 2} \% / 23.2 \% / 13.2 \%$. This work achieves -28.25 dB and -20 dB EVM for a 200 MHz 64-QAM OFDM and a 2 GHz 16-QAM OFDM signals at $27 \mathbf{G H z}$ without DPD and equalization.

articleTitle: A 2.0-to-4.9 ppm/°C Bandgap Voltage Reference with Source-Sink Current Compensation for BMIC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article proposes a bandgap voltage reference (BGR) with source-sink drift dual current compensation, achieving a low temperature coefficient (TC) over the automotive temperature range from -40 to $125{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ with reduced power consumption. It achieves a best TC of $2.0 \mathrm{ppm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, and an average consumption current of $44 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ at room temperature. Moreover, it achieves the $0.04 \% / V$ linear sensitivity (LS) and -60 dB power supply ripple rejection (PSRR) at 1 Hz at room temperature.

articleTitle: Edge-Optimized AI Architecture: MRAM-based Near Memory Computing Core Balancing between Memory Capacity and Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: General-purpose edge neural networks require a lightweight architecture, delivering both suitable memory capacity and compute resources. Typically, the SRAM-based computing-in memory (CIM) architecture is difficult to provide sufficient storage to fulfilling the computing requirements, and various buffers are needed. In this work, we present a novel high-capacity MRAM-based near memory computing (NMC) architecture with configurable computing unit, adeptly striking a balance between the edge network’s demands for storage and computing. It has realized a storage density of $1.49 \mathrm{Mb} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}$ on-chip and an excellent energy efficiency of 6.164 TOPS/W.

articleTitle: A Ultra-low-power Wake-up Wireless Transmitter for Bio-luminescence Detection in Ingestible Capsules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a wake-up transmitter (WuTX) for bio-luminescence detection in ingestible capsules. The WuTX achieves long-term standby operation through sleep and work modes, with dual-mode switching implemented by a wake-up timer (WuTIM). In sleep mode, only the always-on LDO ($L D O_{A o B}$), reference circuits, and WuTIM are activated, the system operates at 0.4 V through $L D O_{A o B}$, leading to a power consumption of just 10 nW. In work mode, all modules are enabled by WuTIM, the system operates at 1.1 V through $L D O_{T X}$. A chirp injection is adopted to shorten the start-up time of the crystal oscillator (XCO), providing a 26 MHz reference frequency within 1.8 ms while consuming only $25.8 \mu \mathrm{~W}$. Then, a narrow pulse injection signal drives the injection-locked ring oscillator (ILRO) to produce a 130 MHz signal. This signal further generates a 910 MHz carrier frequency by an edge combiner (EC). Finally, a switched capacitor power amplifier (SCPA) is adopted to provide a wide output power range. Fabricated in a 40 nm CMOS process, the WuTX can achieve ${- 1 6} \mathrm{d B m}$ output power with a power consumption of 830 $\mu \mathrm{W}$, leading to an energy efficiency up to $15.9 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$.

articleTitle: An Index-free Coding Compression Mechanism for Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have emerged as powerful models in computer vision but their large parameter counts and substantial memory access costs pose challenges for deployment on resource-constrained platforms. This paper proposes an index-free coding compression mechanism for ViTs, designed to enhance compression efficiency and reduce power consumption significantly. Our mechanism incorporates a heuristic clustering-based coding strategy, a dual-aspect coding evaluation method, and a hardware-friendly index-free decoder design. These innovations provide orthogonal improvements to existing compression methods, further enhancing data compression efficiency. Validated through post-layout simulation and synthesis under the TSMC 28nm process, our method achieves a $2 \times$ compression ratio and enhances energy efficiency by $1.99 \times$ compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: A 0.61 nJ/bit Scheduled Wake-Up Transmitter for Wireless Body Area Networks Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a D8PSK quadrature scheduled wake-up transmitter for video/image transmission in typical wireless body area network medical applications. This design includes a scheduled sleep/wake-up controller and a charge pump based high-efficiency power management unit (PMU), and a quadrature up-conversion transmitter. The scheduled sleep/wakeup scheme and power management technique contribute to reduce the power consumption and extend the life-time of a battery-supplied wireless sensor. This design is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS technology, with a maximum output power of $\mathbf{- 0. 5}$ dBm and an average power consumption of 57.7 uW. The data rate for wake-up mode is 9 Mbps in D8PSK modulation scheme. The achieved EVM is $2.81 \% \mathrm{rms}$ with an energy efficiency of $0.61 \mathrm{~nJ} / \mathrm{bit}$.

articleTitle: A 1∼10MHz Cryo-CMOS Analog Baseband Circuit Achieving 50dB Peak Gain for Superconducting Qubit Readout
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper designs a cryogenic CMOS analog baseband (ABB) circuit with a $1 \sim 10 \mathrm{MHz}$ bandwidth and a peak gain of 50 dB, suitable for superconducting qubit readout. It also provides guidance for the design of cryogenic building block circuits. The circuit comprises a three-stage transconductance-transresistance programmable gain amplifier (PGA) and a third-order Gm-C low-pass filter (LPF). In the absence of comprehensive cryogenic circuit design models, self-biased circuits and pseudo-differential $\mathbf{G m}$ units are designed to address the issue of limited voltage headroom caused by increased threshold voltages at cryogenic temperatures (CT). The proposed ABB is fabricated in 28 nm bulk CMOS technology and achieves a gain range from 0 to 50 dB with 2 dB steps, and a bandwidth of $1 \sim 10 \mathrm{MHz}$. The power consumption is $0.43 \mathrm{~mW} / \mathrm{MHz}$ at cryogenic temperatures. Keywords-cryogenic, analog base-band circuit

articleTitle: An Automatic Hardware Generator for CNN Accelerator on FPGA with Efficient Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The field of e dge d eployment of c onvolutional neural networks (CNNs) based on field-programmable g ate a rrays (FPGAs) requires extensive knowledge and complex steps. The advent of the hls 4 ml tool has greatly simplified t his e dge deployment process. However, configuring the r euse factor p arameters within this tool still involves a very cumbersome process. In this paper, we propose an automatic reuse factor predictor based on resource predictors, latency predictors, and an automatic breadth-first search algorithm. Finally, we predict the reuse factors for a CNN with residual structures and compare them with the actual results after implementation on the Xilinx XCU250 FPGA.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Logarithmic-Posit-Based In-SRAM Computing for Neural Network Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an SRAM-based computing-inmemory (SRAM-CIM) macro with logarithmic-posit (LP) data format for energy-efficient multiplication-and-accumulation (MAC) operations. The LP data format simplifies the multiplier to adder in the logarithmic domain while benefiting from the dynamic data expression of Posit to adapt to the tapered data distribution of neural networks (NN). Meanwhile, alignment with bit-wise exponent comparison is proposed to optimize the floating point (FP) adder tree. Experimental results show that the energy efficiency of our proposed LP-based SRAM-CIM is increased by $2.41 \times$ and $3.50 \times$ compared to previous FP-CIM works, and by $1.68 \times$ compared to previous INT-CIM work, all with comparable accuracy loss.

articleTitle: Modeling the Resistance Variation of Heterogeneous Integrated Interconnect Structures under Electrical Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper studies the resistance change caused by temperature rise due to different currents passing through the sample under electrical stress. The device under test (DUT) is an interconnect structure composed of SAC305 (Sn 96.5%, Ag 3.0%, $\mathrm{Cu} 0.5 \%$) and copper, and the experimental temperature set at $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The experiment applied $1 \mathrm{~A} \mathrm{DC}, 2 \mathrm{~A} \mathrm{DC}$ and 2.2 A DC currents to the DUT for a total duration of 510 hours.
