According to the resistance surge phenomenon in the test results, a thermoelectric coupling model is proposed to solve the current temperature-resistance relationship of the interconnect structure, and compared with the test results, the error does not exceed 2%, which verifies its correctness.

articleTitle: +A 112Gbps DSP-Based PAM4 SerDes Receiver with a Wide Band Equalization Tuning AFE in 7nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: this paper presents a 112Gbps DSP-Based PAM4 SerDes receiver with a wide band equalization tuning AFE. The wide band equalization is realized by implementing source degeneration, high-pass branch and inductive peaking. The AFE provides flexible peaking tuning and up to 17.5dB peaking tuning range at Nyquist frequency. With the proposed AFE, the receiver sees eye opening after digital FIR equalization and achieves 6e-9 BER with a 29.6dB insertion loss channel.

articleTitle: An Ising-mTSP Solver Based on the Mixed Simulated Annealing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The min-max multiple traveling salesman problem (minmax mTSP) is one of the most well-known combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). As a non-deterministic polynomial problem, the min-max mTSP can not be efficiently solved by modern Von-Neumann architecture-based computers. In this paper, an Ising-mTSP solver is proposed to efficiently solve the min-max mTSP. A mixed simulated annealing algorithm that combining the distributed simulated annealing and the multi-objective simulated annealing is proposed to accelerate the annealing process and improve the accuracy of the solution. The two phase heuristic method is adopted to reduce the processing time and resources. Furthermore, the corresponding hardware structure is developed.

articleTitle: A Noise-Shaping SAR-assisted Pipelined MASH DT/CT Hybrid DSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a Noise-Shaping SAR-assisted Pipelined MASH DT/CT Hybrid Delta-Sigma Modulator (DSM). Continuous-time (CT) DSMs are known for their anti-aliasing capabilities, but high-order DSMs face stability and dynamic range issues. The proposed architecture overcomes the quantization noise (QN) leakage problem of multi-level noise shaping (MASH), demonstrating significant improvements in power efficiency and robustness against process variations. The modulator is clocked at 800 MHz and consumes 6.7 mW of power achieving 81.5dB DR, 88.2dBc SFDR, and 78.5dB SNDR at a 20 MHz BW.

articleTitle: Electro-Magnetic Field Study on Skin Effect Suppression of Metal/Ferromagnet Superlattice Conductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The emerging superlattice conductors featuring skin effect suppression are attracting growing interests from domains of chip and packaging level high-speed interconnects and network devices. For the first time, a systematical design strategy is concluded from solution of Maxwell equations, guiding selection of materials and parameters to attain desired suppression band and depth at high precision. Developments of materials and processing technics are proposed to extend upper limits of the superlattices.

articleTitle: Device Characteristic-Aware Quantization for eFlash-Based In-Memory Computing SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This study presents an eFlash-based in-memory computing (IMC) SoC leveraging device characteristic-aware quantization to enhance accuracy. A non-uniform quantization method, based on the non-linear characteristics of eFlash devices, is proposed to simplify the control of the number of electrons. Additionally, several channel-wise quantization schemes are introduced, considering the characteristics of the array and data distribution. These methods significantly improve image classification accuracy on the CIFAR-10 dataset using a CNN network, achieving enhancements of $\mathbf{2. 2 \%}, \mathbf{4. 2 \%}, \mathbf{5. 6 \%}$, and $\mathbf{1 4. 4} \%$ compared to baseline models.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: Low-Temperature SiO2/SiO2 Wafer Direct Bonding by N2 Plasma Activation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Direct bonding is a promising technology in the semiconductor industry for achieving material stack integration. Traditional high-temperature bonding methods can introduce thermal stresses and defects that affect device performance and reliability. This paper proposes a low-temperature SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> wafer bonding technique based on non-oxidizing nitrogen plasma activation. Here, we show that $\mathbf{N}_{2}$ plasma treatment significantly enriches the surface with functional groups, improving the chemical reactivity and surface energy, thus achieving a high bonding strength of $\sim 2.0 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The mechanism of nitrogen plasma activation on surface modification and interfacial bonding was revealed by surface analysis and mechanical strength testing. This study is of great significance for the development of component fabrication, micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) and optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Design and Packaging of a W Band CMOS Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article presents the design and packaging of a W-band CMOS power amplifier (PA). The power amplifier utilizes transformer-based matching networks. A low-loss packaging method is proposed and applied to the power amplifier, accompanied by a co-simulation of the PA’s design and packaging. Measurement results show that the packaged PA achieves a small signal gain of 15 dB and a saturated power of 18 dBm within 90 to 100 GHz, with a maximum power added efficiency of $18 \%$.

articleTitle: A Fast-Settling Hybrid Adaptive On-Off-Delay Compensation for Series-Series Wireless Power Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A resonant regulated rectifier $\left(R^{3}\right)$ with fast-settling hybrid adaptive on/off-delay compensation is proposed for series-series wireless power receivers (RX), enhancing power conversion efficiency (PCE) and power driving capability. The proposed off-delay compensation, based on an offset voltage locking technique, achieves accurate and instant compensation. Additionally, the on-delay compensation, utilizing an edge cross-trigger circuit, provides instant correction with a simple circuit architecture. The proposed RX was implemented in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. Simulation results show a $5-\mathrm{V}$ regulated output with up-to-7W output power. The peak PCE of 94.8% was achieved with the proposed hybrid adaptive on/off-delay compensation.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: Area Efficient Low Power Data Transmission Circuit with Analog Differential Data Selector for CMOS Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an area efficient, low power data transmission circuit for CMOS image sensor (CIS). In this circuit, a novel analog $2: 1$ data selector with differential structure has been proposed, which reduces 62% power consumption and 70% layout area comparing with conventional circuits. The data transmission circuit with serializer and LVDS driver has been designed based on $1 \mathrm{P} 6 \mathrm{M} \quad 0.15 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process with chip area of $2.31 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.34 \mathrm{~mm}$, and it achieves a maximum transmission rate of 1.25Gbps with transmission energy efficiency of $2.88 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit} / \mathrm{pF}$.

articleTitle: A 0.8-V-VIN 3.76-nW 23.1-ppm/°C Low Dropout Regulator Based on Flipped Voltage Follower with Embedded CMOS Voltage Reference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This brief presents an ultra-low power sub-threshold low-dropout (LDO) regulator based on a cascode flipped voltage follower (FVF) with an embedded CMOS voltage reference (ECVR), implemented in $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS technology. The LDO integrates temperature compensation mechanisms into the regulation loop, including a complementary-to-absolute-temperature (CTAT) voltage generator and a proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) voltage generator. Therefore, the regulator achieves an output voltage of 0.6 V with a temperature coefficient of $23.1 \mathrm{ppm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ over a temperature range of $-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, eliminating the need for an additional voltage reference circuit. This design approach effectively reduces both chip area and power consumption. The LDO maintains stability without an output capacitor and supports a maximum load current of 10 mA. Additionally, it operates with a minimum supply voltage as low as 0.8V while consuming only 3.76 nW of total power.

articleTitle: A 1.2-μA SIMO DC-DC Converter with 0.04-mV/mA Cross Regulation under Simultaneous Multi-Channel Loading Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article presents a low-power single-inductor multioutput (SIMO) DC-DC converter with three independent outputs. An asynchronous balanced power-distributive control (BPDC) is proposed to reduce the delay charging period of the channels to mitigate the cross regulation. Implemented in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ BCD technology, the proposed SIMO converter achieves a quiescent current of $1.2 \mu \mathrm{A}$ and a peak efficiency of 91.8%. A power efficiency of 83.9% is measured under $10-\mu \mathrm{A}$ loading current. The measured transient response time is $1.7 \mu \mathrm{s}$ with $0.38-\mathrm{mV} / \mathrm{mA}$ output voltage droop when loading changes from $10 \mu \mathrm{A}$ to 100 mA. Moreover, the cross regulation has minimized to be $0.04 \mathrm{mV} / \mathrm{mA}$ when the load currents of other 2 channels change simultaneously.

articleTitle: A 4-8 GHz Fully-Differential Noise Canceling Low Noise Amplifier in 55-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: in this paper, a two-stage low noise amplifier(LNA) design is proposed in the 55 nm CMOS process that features a Fully-Differential noise canceling LNA(FD-NCLNA) structure as the first stage. The proposed LNA utilizes inductance to optimize gain and noise characteristics at high frequency and achieves a maximum gain of 18.4 dB and a minimum NF result of 2.5 dB within the $4-8 \mathrm{GHz}$ range.

articleTitle: A 64-GBaud 64-QAM Optical Coherent Transmitter with Monolithically Integrated Driver and I/Q Modulator in 45-nm SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an optical coherent transmitter consisting of an analog output stage and two Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZM). For monolithic integration of electrical and optical parts, a Cherry-Hooper-based 3-bit high speed R-2R ladder DAC and a push-pull output driver is realized to achieve high speed pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) signal generation, amplification and electrical-optical connection. The designed MOSFET variable resistors in DAC also provide pre-distortion to compensate nonlinearity of later stages. Simulations results show the combination of DAC, and the output driver achieves over 59 GHz 3-dB bandwidth with differential inputs, permitting 64GBaud PAM-8 signal processing. Implemented in a 45 nm silicon photonic (Si-Ph) CMOS SOI process, the optical transmitter reaches $384 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathbf{s}$ channel speed with $64-Q A M$ modulation, at the electrical power cost of about 600 mW.

articleTitle: A 11.2-17.5 GHz Continuous Class-F Power Amplifier with Balanced 8-Ways Harmonic Tuning Achieving 30.3dBm Pout and 32% PAE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a $11.2-17.5 \mathrm{GHz}$ continuous Class-F power amplifier (PA). A prototype of three-stages cascaded PA with balanced 8 -ways combined harmonic tuning matching network in continuous Class-F is proposed. It realizes on-chip continuous harmonic-termination output network as well as 8ways power combining with low impedance imbalance in ultra-wideband for efficiency/output power boosting and harmonic suppression of the PA. Compact output network with low insertion loss is adopted. The core area of proposed PA is only $0.85 \times 0.75 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ in $0.13 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS SOI process. The results show that the PA achieves a maximum output power of $30.7 \mathrm{dBm}, 3-\mathrm{dB}$ bandwidth from 11.2-17.5GHz, peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 35.2%, $2^{\text {nd }}-/ 3^{\text {rd }}$-order harmonics suppression of $61.1 / 40.8 \mathrm{dBc}$ for 15 GHz fundamental frequency.

articleTitle: A 22nm Variation-Tolerant Clock Duty-Cycle Controller for Mitigating Aging-Induced Clock Duty-Cycle Distortion with Path Replica
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This study proposes a PVTA variation-tolerant adaptive clock duty-cycle controller (DCC) designed to address aging-induced clock duty-cycle distortion (DCD) with clock tree replica and data path replica. The dual-role DCC integrates monitoring and adjustment within a unified framework, offering robust duty-cycle control under variations without specialized calibration. By indirectly monitoring clock and data path replica, this approach overcomes the challenges associated with in-situ monitoring of clock-leaf nodes and provides a reliable foundation to enable DCC. The architecture supports PVTA-calibration-free operation, enabling precise duty-cycle corrections across a frequency range from 250 MHz to 1 GHz. Implemented in a 22 nm PULP CPU, the DCC demonstrates significant improvements in duty-cycle accuracy with an error margin of only 1.1%, while maintaining a rapid response time of 51 cycles at $1 \mathbf{G H z}$.

articleTitle: A Noise Shaping SAR ADC with kT/C Noise Cancellation and Mismatch Error Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The resolution of SAR ADCs is primarily limited by sampling noise, DAC mismatch, and comparator noise. This work presents a noise-shaping SAR ADC design that addresses all these error sources. Sampling noise is mitigated using a kT/C noise cancellation technique combined with resampling. DAC mismatch is managed through data-weighted averaging (DWA) and mismatch error shaping (MES), while comparator noise is reduced using a second-order passive noise-shaping (NS) technique. Designed in a 28nm CMOS process, the ADC achieves 86.8 dB SNDR across a 2.8 MHz bandwidth with a power consumption of 3.8 mW.

articleTitle: A Wide Dynamic Range Burst Mode Transimpedance Amplifier in BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a burst mode transimpedance amplifier (BM-TIA) suitable for applications in passive optical network (PON). Hybrid automatic gain control (AGC) structure is employed to achieve high sensitivity of -33.5 dBm and wide dynamic range up to 26.5 dBm. Fabricated in $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ SiGe BiCMOS process, the proposed BM-TIA achieves $76.94 \mathrm{~dB} \Omega$ transimpedance gain and a bandwidth of 7.4 GHz. It consumes 132 mW of power and occupies a chip area of $\mathbf{0. 9 2 2} \mathrm{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$.

articleTitle: A 40-nA Quiescent Current Buck Converter With ACC/AOT Dual-Mode Control and Fast-Transient Response for IoT Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A dual-mode ultra-low quiescent current DC-DC buck converter is proposed to achieve high efficiency over a wide load range from $1 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ to 100 mA. The circuit employs adaptive clock control (ACC) for light load and adaptive on-time control (AOT) for heavy load. Additionally, the circuit introduces a load transient enhancing comparator to achieve minimal voltage undershoot, along with fast recovery time. The converter is implemented in a 180 nm process and operates with an input voltage of 2.4 V to 3.3 V and an output of 1.5 V. It achieves over 90% efficiency across full load range, with a peak efficiency of 97.3% at 2.4 V input. The total quiescent consumption is 40 nA and it achieves an undershoot voltage of 43 mV and a recovery time of $5.3 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ when the load current steps from $10 \mu$ A to 100 mA.

articleTitle: Thermal Stress and Impact Factors for the Embedded Silicon Bridge (EMIB) in a Chiplet Package
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this study, thermal stresses in critical components of an embedded silicon bridge (EMIB) within a chiplet package were analyzed using the finite element analysis (FEA). The stress impact factors, including bump diameter-to-pitch ratios, bump distribution patterns, and EMIB thickness, were investigated through stress analysis. The results reveal that the stress is allievated with a bump diameter-to-pitch ratio of 0.3, a peripheral bump distribution effectively reduces stress, and a reduction in EMIB thickness contributes to a decrease in stress. However, the number of EMIBs and their aspect ratios have a minimal impact on stress, offering design flexibility.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: A 3∼45 V input and 3.1μ A quiescent current LDO with fast transient response for automotive electronics application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a wide input and low power LDO with fast transient response for automotive electronic applications. This design employs impedance adaptive compensation and load pseudo-ESR zero tracking techniques, achieving excellent frequency and transient performance over a wide load range. The LDO chip is fabricated in a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ BCD process. The measurement results show the input voltage range is from 3 V to 45 V, and the output voltage range is from 1.22 V to 5 V with a quiescent current of $3.1 \mu \mathrm{~A}$. The load regulation is 0.07 $\mathrm{mV} / \mathrm{mA}$ with the load steps from 1 mA to 300 mA. The power supply rejection ratio of the chip are 80 dB at 10 kHz and 20 dB at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: A Lightweight 3D D2D Interface for Active Interposer Chiplet Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a standardised, power-efficient and low-latency die-to-die (D2D) physical layer interface for active interposer and chiplet vertical interconnect. It realises the interoperation between chiplet and interposer in 28 nm and 40 nm respectively. To control the overhead, it adopts self-timed and parallel interface architecture with limited data rate and uses a lightweight deskew scheme. Post-layout simulation shows that this 3D D2D interface achieves a high data rate of 4Gbps per lane, a high energy efficiency of $0.74 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$ and $0.81 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$ in two directions respectively and a short latency of 3.2 ns.

articleTitle: A Simplified Polynomial Behavioral Model for Linearization of Envelope Tracking Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, a simplified polynomial behavioral model is proposed to improve the linearity of an envelope tracking power amplifier (ET-PA). Theoretical analysis reveals that the third-order and the fifth-order intermodulation (IM) components can be reduced if properly shaping the dynamic drain voltage. Based on a two-tone signal test, the proposed model is constructed for the ET-PA, and then applied to predict the optimal shaping function for linearity enhancement. With aid of the proposed model, the ET-PA achieves a reduction of $8.2 \mathrm{~dB} / 9.4 \mathrm{~dB}$ at the lower and upper third-order IM components, and a 6 dB back-off power-added efficiency (PAE) higher than $40 \%$.

articleTitle: A Voltage Domain Code Division Multiplex Based Analog Front End For Energy-Efficient Multi-channel Bio-potential Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a voltage domain code division multiplex based analog front end for multi-channel bio-potential acquisition. Implemented with switched-capacitor multiplying digital-to-analog converters, multiple biopotential signals are modulated simultaneously into a single channel and amplified, which reduces hardware cost and power consumption. Furthermore, chopper is used to reduce the low frequency noise from the amplifier. The proposed circuit structure is verified in an 8-channel acquisition system with 180 nm CMOS process. The simulation results demonstrate an inter-channel crosstalk of -64 dB with an overall voltage gain of 26 dB, input referred noise of $1.54 \mu \mathrm{~V}$, while the entire system dissipates $8 \mu \mathrm{~W}$/channel.

articleTitle: Compact Model of Borophene Field Effect Transistors for Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Benefiting from the high carrier mobility, the two-dimensional (2D) material borophene is promising to be used in high-speed applications. This paper investigates entirely the I/V characteristics of a borophene field-effect transistor (BFET) device and proposes a corresponding SPICE-compatible model for circuit design. Technology computer aided design (TCAD) tool is employed to investigate the I/V characteristics of BFET, including subthreshold swing (SS) and Ion/Ioff ratio. The simulation results show that the SS of BFET is lower than that of the conventional MOSFET while the Ion/Ioff ratio of BFET is higher. The electrical properties of BFET are integrated in a behavioral model for circuit design. The proposed model has been implemented in an inverter circuit to evaluate the performance improvement of BFET.

articleTitle: Mixed-dimensional Integration for Tetrachromatic Optoelectronic Synaptic Devices Based on 2D/3D WSe2-GaN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Mixed-dimensional heterostructures (MDHs) open up new opportunity for next-generation optoelectronic synaptic devices by simulating the integrated functions of the human visual system. In this work, we proposed a dual-channel WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GaN 2D/3D integrated optoelectronic synaptic device exhibiting synaptic characteristics to broadband wavelengths in ultraviolet-visible range and demonstrating a comprehensive set of emulating basic optoelectronic synaptic characteristics. Notably, the device’s plasticity is tunable at different wavelengths, which is attributed to the different photogenerated carrier dynamics in the WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-GaN channel under ultraviolet and visible light stimulation. This work proposes a significant milestone of MDH-based artificial synapses solely utilizing their individual optoelectronic features, which is attractive toward scaled-up neuromorphic architectures.

articleTitle: An 800MS/s Continuous-Time Pipeline ADC with Switchable FLASH and RDAC for Background Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-time pipeline ADC with background calibration. The calibration is based on split structure. A switchable FLASH and RDAC is proposed to achieve the shift of residue modes compatible with PN injection for continuous input. Additionally, the taps of the digital reconstruction FIR are iterated by LMS. An 800MS/s 100MHz BW two-stage continuous-time pipeline ADC using the proposed calibration method is implemented in a 65 nm CMOS technology, achieving SNDR of 67.6dB with 13.09MHz -2.5dBFS input. There is only 1-dB deterioration in SNDR compared to the classical foreground calibration with noisemin algorithm. However, this method can achieve background calibration with much lower hardware cost.

articleTitle: Fourier-LSTM on the Edge: Elevating Genome Sequencing Performance on the Portable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Genome sequencing has evolved from Sanger to advanced third-generation technologies, yet challenges such as limited read lengths and high costs remain. This paper introduces Fourier-LSTM, a hardware-efficient block integrating Fourier transformations with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This approach enhances handling long repetitive sequences and structural variations to improve nanopore sequencing accuracy. Notably, deploying Fourier-LSTM on the embedded RK3588 device significantly reduces power consumption and costs, making it ideal for real-time, portable genomic applications.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network based Model for Power GaN HEMTs down to 4.2K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation and an artificial neural network (ANN)-based modeling of the DC characteristics of power GaN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) operating at temperatures ranging from 300 K to 4.2 K. The proposed ANN architecture accurately captures the correlation between electrical properties. More importantly, based on the optimized ANN architecture, we further predict the electrical performance of untrained devices fabricated on the same wafer. The predictive results show nearly perfect matching with the experimental results in the DC model, particularly at cryogenic temperatures, featuring a root-mean-square (RMS) error of less than 1%.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Pulse Signal Detection Based on a Dual-transistor Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a novel method for the detection of ultrafast pulse signals, utilizing an AOS transistor-based 2T0C DRAM unit. By leveraging the ultrafast programming capability and long retention time of the 2 TOC unit, it can extend the duration of the signal, thereby achieving stable detection. The experimental results demonstrate that the fabricated InAlZnO 2T0C unit is capable of effectively capturing high-speed signals as short as 25 nanoseconds and possesses over $10^{8}$ amplifications in the time domain for pulse signals. The stable and highly efficient detection method based on the 2 TOC unit holds promise as an ideal choice for future fast signal detection.

articleTitle: Truncation Error Compensation Technique with Auxiliary Noise Shaping Filter in CT DSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a truncation error compensation technique with auxiliary noise shaping filter in continuous-time (CT) delta-sigma modulator (DSM) with digital truncation. The truncation error compensation filter is used to reduce the quantization noise with low latency in feedback loop. An auxiliary noise shaping filter is proposed to suppress the truncation error leakage due to the mismatch between digital and analog filter. A CT DSM with proposed techniques achieves a SNDR of 75.7 dB and a DR of 78 dB with 25 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Mixer-BBPD-Based Real-Time I/Q Calibration Loop for High-Speed Ring-Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a digital-intensive real-time in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) calibration loop for mm-wave ring-oscillators (ROs) by adopting a fully-symmetric mixer-based bang-bang phase detector (BBPD). The proposed calibration loop is both area- and power-efficient, making it highly suitable for on-chip integration. Implemented in $28-\text{nm}$ CMOS, the proposed automatic I/Q calibration achieves high accuracy $\lt0.5^{\circ}$ for an RO operating at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: A Low-noise CTIA-based Non-contact PPG Sensor Analog Front End with Chopping and RDAC Compensation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-noise AFE based on a capacitive transimpedance amplifier (CTIA) for wearable PPG sensors. By separating noise from the PPG signal, the proposed AFE applies chopping technique to the CTIA for reducing flicker noise and input-referred offset. Resistive DAC (RDAC) is adopted to substitute the conventional current DAC to suppress the noise in the dual compensation loop by replacing the high transistor noise with the lower resistor thermal noise. In $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS, the proposed AFE under 1.2 V consumes $68 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ power with an equivalent input-referred noise of $\mathbf{1 5. 3 2}$ pArms. Compared with the related works, the proposed AFE reduces noise by 45.3% ~ 83.3% with comparable power consumption and silicon area.

articleTitle: A 930MHz Low Phase Noise MEMS Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 930 MHz complementary cross-coupled MEMS oscillator with Darlington cell is proposed to effectively reduce the power consumption and optimize phase noise of the circuit in this paper. The circuit is designed using SMIC 55 nm CMOS process with a phase noise of $\mathbf{- 1 3 6. 5} \mathbf{~ d B c} / \mathbf{H z}$ and Figure of Merit (FOM) of 224.6 at 100 kHz offset frequency, an overall circuit power consumption of $134 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ at 1.2 V supply voltage, a start-up time of $14.8 \mu \mathrm{~s}$, and a core circuit layout area of $85 \times 87 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: BISHENG: A 49.38PPM Flexible Multi-Function Printer SoC in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Innovative AI functions and imaging algorithms are important for multi-function printers (MFP) to provide good user experience. However, prior printer system on chips (SoC) using hardwired hardware or customized processors have limited flexibility and programmability. This paper proposes a flexible MFP SoC called BISHENG, which uses customized RISC-V processors and a hybrid interconnect with sequential pipeline and partial crossbar. The chip was fabricated in 28 nm CMOS. Experiment result shows that it can achieves 49.38 pages per minute (PPM) in prototype printer with a typical power 2.55 W. Keywords-System on Chip, Multi-Function Printer, Document Image Processing, On-Chip Network

articleTitle: A Wide-Load-Range High-PSR Capless Low-Dropout Regulator with Adaptive Supply-Ripple Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: For higher power density, the switching frequency of pre-stage DC-DC converters has evolved to be greater than 1MHz, requesting low dropout (LDO) regulators must have high power supply rejection (PSR) over a wider frequency range. In this paper, we propose a capless LDO regulator with an adaptive negative capacitance generation circuit to achieve high PSR over wide load and frequency ranges. The proposed LDO regulator is designed using a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process. Simulations results show that the proposed LDO regulator achieves greater than -60dB PSR at 100kHz and greater than -40dB PSR at 1 MHz over a load range of $500 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ to 50mA, with a total on-chip capacitance of only 105pF.

articleTitle: Design of a High Jitter Harmonic Injected Ring Oscillator for Entropy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: in the field of modern cryptography and-information security, the generation of random numbers is crucial, with the quality of the entropy source being paramount. This study explores the design of Ring Oscillator (RO)-based entropy sources, noted for their high manufacturability and ease of integration. However, the jitter produced by naive ROs is insufficient for high-quality entropy. We propose a design that significantly enhances jitter performance through the introduction of a harmonic injection path. This approach maintains high synthesizability while incurring only modest increases in area and power consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that the modified RO,fa bricated using a 180 nm process, elevated the average min-entropy from $0.058 / \mathrm{bit}$ to 0.351/bit, offering new insights and substantial support for the development of high-quality random number generators.

articleTitle: A 4x16 Arrayed Current Sensing Front-End Chip for DNA Sequencing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a $4 \times 16$ arrayed current sensing front-end chip design for fast DNA sequencing. The chip includes 16 capacitive trans-impedance amplifiers and 16 voltage-to-time conversion circuits. This reduces the array sensing time to $40 \ \mu \text{s}$, as the sensing time of single DNA base is $10 \ \mu \text{s}$, with a current resolution as low as 5 pA, the conversion accuracy and efficiency are greatly improved. The chip is designed and fabricated in 180-nm CMOS process and Operates at a voltage of 1.8 V. The results show that the current sensing rang is from 10 pA to 200 pA, which refers to a nanopore resistance ranging from $600 \text{M} \Omega$ to $10 \text{G} \Omega$.
